newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq prints photos of missing Kuwaitis and others.
newsitem.headline: Iraq prints photos of missing Kuwaitis and others.

text.p: An Iraqi group plans to publicise the pictures of Kuwaitis who went missing during their country's occupation by Iraq in an attempt to trace the people, the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya reported on Monday.

The paper, quoting a source at the Iraqi committee trying to trace the missing Kuwaitis, said pictures of the missing would be hung throughout the country in public places in an attempt to elicit information from Iraqi citizens.
"The committee has started the printing of murals containing pictures, names and the nationalities of all those who went missing in action...," the paper said.

"The committee urges citizens or anyone who has information on the said MIAs to supply it to the headquarters of the Human Rights Organisation in Baghdad or Red Crescent societies in the provinces," Jumhouriya said.
The Iraqi Human Rights Organisation set up the committe last year and also included representatives of the Iraqi parliament, the Red Crescent and the Iraqi Lawyers Union.
The paper also said Baghdad had given to Kuwait information on 300 of the 600 people Kuwait says are being held in Iraq.
Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990 and were ousted in the 1991 Gulf War.
Kuwait and its ally the United States say a full accounting of the missing is one of several conditions Iraq must meet before economic sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion can be lifted.
Iraq said it has freed all those captured but has promised to look at the issue again.
